info.title: goo observability API
info.description: Current development API served by one Go process. Browser paths under /api and unprefixed API paths dispatch to the same handlers, admission controls and state. No proxy or JSON reserialization boundary. Wire-shape schemas describe encoding, not all domain validation. Semantic constraints, custody and source effects remain authoritative in Go. Unknown input fields are rejected; null and omitted fields can decode and then fail domain validation. No authentication is implemented by this lab; cancellation IDs are local capabilities, not authorization.

get.description: Derived metadata search over immutable captures, literal case-insensitive title containment, optional exact kind/signal/environment, capture-time order. No telemetry reads or payload bodies. 10,000 nonreserved directory entries (two known index directories separately reserved), 16 MiB aggregate metadata, 64 KiB per metadata entry and 8 MiB retained summary JSON; missing index/budget refusal is 503. Metadata checksum and payload stat stamps do not establish payload content integrity; reopen and explicit rebuild verify full contents. Cursors bind query, admitted catalog IDs and metadata digests; changed scope/catalog is 400. Omitted environment matches any; present-empty matches exact empty. Direct ID reopen keeps its independent limits.

exploration.CapturePage.description: Exclusive full capture delivery page. Receipt/question/result arms agree before family semantic admission. Metadata-only references are a separate boundary; historical source plans and custody remain family-owned.

exploration.CapturedRecord.description: Server-resolved immutable capture evidence with original receipt/read clock and full versus retained counts. Hashes identify bytes, not physical events or authenticated provenance.

exploration.CountedValuesResult.description: Exactly two bounded aggregate reads: complete count then complete string groups, with separate read clocks and content bases. changed_between_reads retains diagnostic observations but must not drive population actions. state.description: Metadata capability state, including candidate. Not a service-health verdict, observed server count or semantic-convention conformance assertion.

families.description: Opt-in bounded family descriptors. HTTP/RPC/DB/messaging candidate metadata must be confirmed by the executable question before treating counts as observed; no hidden source read or fallback is performed by this planner.

nativeCapability.description: service-per-stream means this policy supports typed gauges, monotonic counters and explicit duration histograms. Other native families and entity bindings remain unavailable. Empty native options do not prove no metric observations.

nativeOptionsOmitted.description: Optional positive count of supported native options excluded by the 128-option display bound after exact-stream expansion. Omitted/zero preserves legacy wire bytes.

profile.description: Selected all-spans, http-server, http-client, rpc-server-current, rpc-server, db-client, messaging-consumer or messaging-producer family for explicit profile requests; absent for the generic overview.

Auto prefers eligible HTTP, current RPC, then legacy RPC before DB; no new source probe is implied.

httpServerObserved.description: Optional advisory positive hint from already-held, same-scope span observations. false/omitted means no positive hint, not HTTP absence; no new probe or semantic-convention compliance claim is implied.

messagingConsumerObserved.description: Optional advisory positive hint from already-held, same-scope Consumer spans with nonempty messaging.system on the same row. false/omitted is unknown, not absence, delivery success, acknowledgement or broker health. A compatible processing-duration histogram can independently admit the consumer family; it remains a separate population.

messagingProducerObserved.description: Optional advisory positive hint from already-held, same-scope Producer spans with nonempty messaging.system on the same row. false/omitted is unknown, not absence or delivery success. Consumer has automatic precedence; processing metrics never admit the producer family.

profile.description: Optional auto, all-spans, http-server, http-client, rpc-server-current, rpc-server, db-client, messaging-consumer or messaging-producer selection. Outgoing HTTP is explicit-only and pinned to OTel v1.45.0; actual record widgets require Client kind and nonempty current http.request.method. Destination, method, literal reported port and response status have separate bounded queries; missing/empty values remain distinct. Counts are Client-span records, not attempts, unique requests, callee identity or remote health. Native http.client.request.duration histograms in exact seconds have independently checked per-stream bindings. They do not enable this record lens or prove Client spans; record-profile selection does not grant native binding authority. Omitted/empty/null selects the generic record overview. Automatic precedence is HTTP, current RPC, legacy RPC, DB client, messaging consumer, messaging producer, then All spans. Current RPC is pinned to OTel semantic conventions v1.45.0: positive same-row Server/rpc.system.name hint plus current-key metadata, or a compatible rpc.server.call.duration histogram in seconds. Method is optional; missing and empty method groups remain distinct. Legacy RPC requires its independent rpc.system/rpc.method population or millisecond duration instrument. Flat keys alone are candidates, not observations; no alias union, conformance claim or hidden probe.

rpcServerCurrentObserved.description: Optional advisory positive hint from an already-held same-scope Server span with a nonempty rpc.system.name on that same row. rpc.method is conditional, not required for this witness. False/omitted means unknown, not absence or conformance. Current RPC uses its own pinned profile; no legacy key fallback or new probe.

rpcServerObserved.description: Optional advisory positive hint from already-held, same-scope Server span observations with nonempty legacy rpc.system and rpc.method on the same row. false/omitted is unknown, not RPC absence or conformance. HTTP and current RPC have automatic precedence; this does not authorize a probe.

x-contract-notes: Go accepts any request Content-Type; application/json is the supported client encoding.
Browser /api and unprefixed API requests have the same byte limits, headers, cancellation and streaming semantics.
JSON receive is bounded to 15 seconds and interrupted by request cancellation; successful decoding clears the receive deadline before source/response work.
Operation GET validation uses http.Error text/plain with JSON-looking text; /api preserves that status, type and body.
Tail early JSON errors omit Cache-Control; streaming responses set no-store and X-Accel-Buffering: no.
Health is process liveness only; it does not query ClickHouse or certify telemetry ingestion.
No generated handlers, semantic validator replacement, API stability guarantee or new authorization layer is introduced.

Ordinary record Query input is a closed non-null graph: exact field names and one predicate arm; missing zero defaults remain permitted. Other input families retain their independently documented null policies.
